LESSON: READING 9.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READER

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What marks the climax of a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the sequence of events in a text
2. appreciate reading works of art for information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 9.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READER
This lesson teaches Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader for Grade 7 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. explain the sequence of events in a text
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate reading works of art for information and enjoyment
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader above.
2. Explain Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

2. appreciate reading works of art for information and enjoyment
